Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects of a unitary fusion category
$\mathcal C$ ([[def-qc-tqc-unitary-fusion-category]]). The **fusion
multiplicity** is

$$N_{ab}^c:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c),$$

and the corresponding **fusion multiplicity space** is

$$V_{ab}^c:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c).$$

Since $c$ is absolutely simple
([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]), each $f,g\in V_{ab}^c$ has a unique scalar
$\langle f,g\rangle$ satisfying
$f\circ g^\dagger=\langle f,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$. This fixes the
inner-product convention to be linear in the first variable. The next local
theorem proves that this pairing is positive definite. No multiplicity-free
assumption is made: $N_{ab}^c$ may be any nonnegative integer.

Let $a,b,c,d$ be simple charges in a unitary fusion category, and put
$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique
empty $0\times0$ matrix.

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects in a unitary braided fusion category, with
braiding $c_{a,b}:a\otimes b\to b\otimes a$ as in [[def-braiding]]. The typed
channel-exchange map on $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$ is the
pullback

$$\mathcal R_{ab}^c(f):=f\circ c_{a,b}^{-1}\in V_{ba}^c.$$

Choose orthonormal bases in the two multiplicity spaces. The matrix of
$\mathcal R_{ab}^c$ in these bases is the **R-symbol** $R_{ab}^c$. This
pullback convention fixes the orientation of the coordinate exchange; reversing
the braiding orientation replaces it by the inverse convention. If the spaces
are zero-dimensional, the braiding isomorphism identifies both with $0$ and
the R-symbol is the unique empty $0\times0$ matrix.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $(-)^{\vee\vee}$ be the monoidal endofunctor of
[[thm-the-double-dual-is-a-monoidal-functor]].

A **pivotal structure** on a rigid monoidal category is an isomorphism of
monoidal functors

$$a:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^{\vee\vee}.$$

Equivalently, it is a natural family of isomorphisms
$a_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X^{\vee\vee}$ such that

$$a_{X\otimes Y}=a_X\otimes a_Y,\qquad a_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$$

after transporting along the monoidal structure of the double-dual functor.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

derivations.claim: Let $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{0,1\}$, with $0=\mathbf1$, $1=\eta$, and a third simple $D$. Set $ab=a+b$ for $a,b\in G$, $aD=Da=D$, and $DD=0\oplus1$. Objects are finite ordered sums of these simples, Hom spaces are the corresponding complex matrix blocks, dagger is ordinary matrix adjoint, and tensor on morphisms is the block tensor/convolution induced by the fusion sums. Order the summands of $DD$ as $(0,1)$. Every nonzero elementary multiplicity is one, with specified canonical summand inclusion $i_{ab}^c$ and retraction $p_{ab}^c=(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger$, and multiplicity coordinate $\mu=1$; impossible channels have multiplicity zero. This fixes the bases before any coefficient is calculated.

Put $d=\sqrt2$, $\chi(a,b)=(-1)^{ab}$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$ and $\tau=\kappa/d$. Take identity unit constraints. For $a,b,c\in G$, define the entire associator by $\alpha_{a,b,c}=\alpha_{a,b,D}=\alpha_{D,a,b}=1$, $\alpha_{a,D,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $\alpha_{D,a,D}|_z=\chi(a,z)$ for $z\in G$, and $\alpha_{D,D,D}[f,e]=\tau\chi(e,f)$ for $e,f\in G$. The maps $\alpha_{a,D,D}$ and $\alpha_{D,D,a}$ have coefficient one on the equal simple output, after relabelling the $DD$ summand by addition of $a$. This specifies the direct-sum permutations as well as their scalars. For fixed total $z$, the target row is $(f,\mu_{bc}^f=1,\mu_{af}^z=1)$ and the source column is $(e,\mu_{ab}^e=1,\mu_{ec}^z=1)$; a coefficient exists only when all four fusion multiplicities are one.

In the ordered channels $(0,1)$ the unique two-dimensional block is $F_D^{DDD}=\frac\kappa d\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Every other admissible block is $1\times1$ and equals $+1$, except $F_D^{\eta D\eta}=F_\eta^{D\eta D}=-1$. Unit-input blocks are identities, and an impossible fixed-total space has the unique $0\times0$ matrix. These real matrices and the summand permutations are orthogonal, so their inverse-transposes give exactly the same coefficients. Hence the object associators of step 2.1 are also the F coefficients in the library's inverse-precomposition convention, with no suppressed transpose, inverse, channel, or multiplicity coordinate.

Write $A_z^{abc}[f,e]$ for those associator coefficients, and set them to zero on inadmissible channels. Start at $(((ab)_e c)_f t)_z$ and end at $(a(b(ct)_g)_h)_z$. The root/root route and the left/root/right route around the pentagon give, respectively, the two sides of $A_z^{e c t}[g,f]A_z^{a b g}[h,e]=\sum_u A_f^{a b c}[u,e]A_z^{a u t}[h,f]A_h^{b c t}[g,u]$. This follows by applying each rotation to the indicated subtrees, retaining every spectator output and multiplicity coordinate. We verify all sixteen placements of group objects and $D$ in this indexed equation, rather than using a classification theorem.

With zero $D$ inputs both pentagon routes have coefficient one. With one $D$ input, the four placements reduce in order to the following equalities: $\begin{array}{c|l}(D,a,b,c)&1=1\\(a,D,b,c)&\chi(a,b+c)=\chi(a,b)\chi(a,c)\\(a,b,D,c)&\chi(a+b,c)=\chi(a,c)\chi(b,c)\\(a,b,c,D)&1=1\end{array}$. They hold for all free group labels by bicharacter multiplicativity.

For two $D$ inputs the six placements reduce to $\begin{array}{c|l}(D,D,a,b)&1=1\\(D,a,D,b)&\chi(a,x+b)=\chi(a,x)\chi(a,b)\\(D,a,b,D)&\chi(a,z)\chi(b,z)=\chi(a+b,z)\\(a,D,D,b)&1=1\\(a,D,b,D)&\chi(b,a+y)=\chi(a,b)\chi(b,y)\\(a,b,D,D)&1=1\end{array}$. Here $x$ is the preceding $DD$ output, and $z$ or $a+y$ is the total group output; admissibility forces these labels in the indexed equation. There is exactly one admissible term in its sum over $u$. All six identities follow from symmetry and multiplicativity of $\chi$.

With three $D$ inputs, let $a$ be the group input and $x,y$ the initial and final corresponding two-$D$ output labels. The four placements give $\begin{array}{c|l}(D,D,D,a)&\tau\chi(x,a)\chi(x,y)=\tau\chi(x,a+y)\\(D,D,a,D)&\tau\chi(x,y)=\tau\chi(x+a,y)\chi(a,y)\\(D,a,D,D)&\tau\chi(x,y)=\chi(a,x)\tau\chi(x,a+y)\\(a,D,D,D)&\tau\chi(x,y)\chi(a,y)=\tau\chi(x+a,y)\end{array}$. The middle associator forces each shifted label $x+a$ or $y+a$. Multiplicativity, symmetry and $\chi^2=1$ prove every entry for all free channel labels.

With four $D$ inputs, let $x$ be the initial $DD$ channel, $y$ the final $DD$ channel and $z\in G$ the total. The short route has coefficient $\delta_{y,x+z}$. The long route has coefficient $\tau^2\sum_{u\in G}\chi(x,u)\chi(u,z)\chi(u,y)=\tau^2\sum_u(-1)^{u(x+y+z)}=2\tau^2\delta_{y,x+z}=\delta_{y,x+z}$, since $2\tau^2=1$. Steps 5.1–8.1 exhaust all sixteen placements, every free group/channel label, and every pentagon entry; a nonexistent fusion path gives an empty equality. Every unit-input coefficient agrees with the identity unitor, so the triangle holds. The orthogonal F matrices and ordinary block dagger now give a unitary monoidal category.

Set $u(0)=1$, $u(1)=i$ and choose a unit-modulus $\beta$ with $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. Define all object braiding coefficients by $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$ for $a,b\in G$, $c_{a,D}=c_{D,a}=u(a)$, and $c_{D,D}^g=v(g)=\beta/u(g)$ for $g\in G$. This covers every channel, including units, and all entries have modulus one. Expanding the two hexagons in the normal summand bases reduces their independent equations to $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $u(a+b)=u(a)u(b)\chi(a,b)$, $u(a)v(a+b)=\chi(a,b)v(b)$, $u(a)^2=\chi(a,a)$, and $\tau\sum_{c\in G}\chi(a+b,c)u(c)=\chi(a,b)v(a)v(b)$.

For completeness, the all-group hexagon is bicharacter multiplicativity; the placements $abD$ and $aDb$ give $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$; $Dab$ gives the quadratic equation for $u$; $DDa$ and $DaD$ give the transport equation for $v$; $aDD$ gives $u(a)^2=\chi(a,a)$; and $DDD$ gives the final equation of step 9.1 entry by entry. In that last case the full matrix equality is $A\operatorname{diag}(u)A=\operatorname{diag}(v)A\operatorname{diag}(v)$ with $A=\tau(\chi(a,b))_{a,b}$; cancelling one $\tau$ and combining the character factors gives the displayed sum. The other hexagon reverses these placements and replaces $\chi$ by $\chi^{-1}$, so it gives the same five equations because $\chi=\chi^{-1}$ and both mixed braidings are $u$. This accounts for all eight typed summand patterns of each hexagon.

The only nontrivial quadratic case is $u(1+1)=1=i^2(-1)$, and the nontrivial transport cases are $iv(1)=v(0)$ and $iv(0)=-v(1)$. For the last equation of step 9.1 the four pairs $(a,b)$ give $\begin{array}{c|l}(0,0)&\tau(1+i)=\beta^2\\(1,0),(0,1)&\tau(1-i)=-i\beta^2\\(1,1)&\tau(1+i)=-(-i\beta)^2=\beta^2\end{array}$. Each follows from $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. Thus both hexagons hold in every channel; none of the braiding data has been inferred solely from a two-channel braid relation.

Let $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. At $\kappa=1$, $\beta_+=s$, inverse pullback gives the complete table $R_{0a}^a=R_{a0}^a=1$, $R_{\eta\eta}^0=-1$, $R_{\eta D}^D=R_{D\eta}^D=-i$, $R_{DD}^0=s^{-1}=e^{-\pi i/8}$ and $R_{DD}^\eta=is^{-1}=e^{3\pi i/8}$. At $\kappa=-1$, $\beta_-=-s^{-3}$, the unit/group/mixed entries are identical, while $R_{DD}^0=-s^3$ and $R_{DD}^\eta=s^{-1}$. Every displayed elementary multiplicity index is one, and a nonexistent channel is empty. These are pullback matrices of $f\mapsto f\circ c_{a,b}^{-1}$, rather than object coefficients with only selected phases inverted.

For a group simple $a$, take $\operatorname{coev}_a=i_{aa}^0$ and $\operatorname{ev}_a=p_{aa}^0$. For $D$, take $\operatorname{coev}_D=\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$ and $\operatorname{ev}_D=\kappa\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$. The $D$ snake scalar is $\kappa d(F_D^{DDD})_{0,0}=\kappa d\tau=1$, and reflection proves the other snake; group snakes have scalar one. Thus every object is rigid and the normalized FS sign of $D$ is $\kappa$. Choose right coevaluation $\kappa\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$ and right evaluation $\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$ for $D$; both positive left/right dimensions are $d$, although $\operatorname{ev}_D\operatorname{coev}_D=\kappa d$. The dimension and FS of $\eta$ are one. On a finite sum, the candidate left/right trace is $\sum_a d_a\operatorname{Tr}(M_a)$, where $d_0=d_\eta=1$ and $d_D=d$; we verify its pivotal compatibility explicitly below.

Let $E_c=i_{ab}^cp_{ab}^c$. Inserting the normalized $a$ cup, rotating by $\alpha_{a,a,b}$, applying $E_c$, rotating back and using the positive $a$ cap gives $\operatorname{ptr}_a(E_c)=d_a|A_b^{a a b}[c,0]|^2 1_b=(d_c/d_b)1_b$. Closing $b$ similarly gives $\operatorname{ptr}_b(E_c)=d_b|A_a^{a b b}[0,c]|^2 1_a=(d_c/d_a)1_a$. The entire nonunit calculation is $\begin{array}{c|cc}(a,b;c)&\operatorname{ptr}_a&\operatorname{ptr}_b\\(\eta,\eta;0)&1&1\\(\eta,D;D)&1&d\\(D,\eta;D)&d&1\\(D,D;0)&1/d&1/d\\(D,D;\eta)&1/d&1/d\end{array}$. The first three rows use scalar F entries of modulus one; the last two use $|\tau|^2=1/2$ and $d/2=1/d$. Unit rows are identity traces. In particular all FS signs occur twice and cancel.

Relative to these left duals the standard-conjugate comparison is $j_a=(\operatorname{coev}_a^\dagger\otimes1_{a^{**}})\alpha^{-1}(1_a\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{a^*})$, with typed dual comparisons and unitors inserted. It equals one on a group simple and $d\tau=\kappa$ on $D$. Direct sums use their orthogonal summand inclusions. Iterating the last-vertex calculation of step 14.1 on fusion-path matrix units gives zero off the diagonal and the endpoint dimension on the diagonal; the pentagon makes it tree-independent. These units span every Hom block, and the weighted matrix pairing is nondegenerate. The fusion-dimension equations $d_ad_b=\sum_cN_{ab}^cd_c$ and those same units prove tensor multiplicativity of the trace. Thus the left/right closures both equal $\sum_ad_a\operatorname{Tr}(M_a)$; this is the trace produced by the dualities, rather than an independently assigned dimension function. The following typed tensorator calculation verifies monoidality of $j$ without assuming a canonical positive pivot.

Choose the left dual of a direct sum by its orthogonal simple summands. Its contravariant tensorator $q_{a,b}:b^*\otimes a^*\longrightarrow(a\otimes b)^*$ is uniquely characterized by $\operatorname{ev}_{a\otimes b}(q_{a,b}\otimes1_{a\otimes b})=E_{a,b}$, where $E_{a,b}$ is folded evaluation: reassociate $(b^*\otimes a^*)\otimes(a\otimes b)$ to $b^*\otimes((a^*\otimes a)\otimes b)$, evaluate the middle $a$ pair and then the outer $b$ pair. Uniqueness follows from the two snakes. This fixes all types before taking its channel scalars.

Put $k_a=1$ for $a\in G$ and $k_D=\kappa$. On a canonical $c$ summand, evaluation of both sides of step 16.1 after the $c$ cup gives $q_{a,b}^c=\frac{k_ak_b}{k_c}\sqrt{\frac{d_ad_b}{d_c}}A_0^{b a c}[b,c]A_b^{a a b}[c,0]$. Indeed the first rotation takes $((ba)_c(ab)_c)_0$ to $b(a(ab)_c)$ with coefficient $A_0^{b a c}[b,c]$; the inverse right rotation makes the inner $aa$ channel vacuum with coefficient $A_b^{a a b}[c,0]$. The two evaluations contribute $k_a\sqrt{d_a}k_b\sqrt{d_b}$, the initial $c$ cup contributes $\sqrt{d_c}$, and its comparison cap/cup has scalar $k_cd_c$. Their quotient is the stated formula, derived entirely from the specified dualities and F data.

The complete channel computation is $\begin{array}{c|cccc}(a,b;c)&q_{a,b}^c&\nu_{a,b}^c&j_c&j_aj_b\\(0,0;0)&1&1&1&1\\(0,\eta;\eta)&1&1&1&1\\(\eta,0;\eta)&1&1&1&1\\(0,D;D)&1&1&\kappa&\kappa\\(D,0;D)&1&1&\kappa&\kappa\\(\eta,\eta;0)&1&1&1&1\\(\eta,D;D)&1&1&\kappa&\kappa\\(D,\eta;D)&1&1&\kappa&\kappa\\(D,D;0)&\kappa&1&1&1\\(D,D;\eta)&\kappa&1&1&1\end{array}$. For either $DD$ row the two F factors of step 17.1 are $1,\tau$, and the dimension factor is $d$, so $q=d\tau=\kappa$. In mixed rows both F factors, the dimension quotient, and $k_ak_b/k_c$ are one; unit/group rows are immediate. All entries are real unit scalars.

The typed double-dual tensorator is $
u_{a,b}:a^{**}\otimes b^{**}\longrightarrow(a\otimes b)^{**}$ with $
u_{a,b}=(q_{a,b}^*)^{-1}q_{b^*,a^*}$. On a $c$ summand its coefficient is $q_{b,a}^c/q_{a,b}^c=1$, as recorded in step 18.1. The equality of that table's last columns therefore proves $j_{a\otimes b}=
u_{a,b}(j_a\otimes j_b)$ on all ten admissible channels. Scalar simple components give naturality, chosen sum duals give additivity, and pairwise monoidality extends to arbitrary products by coherence of the canonical dual tensorator. Together with steps 13.1–15.1 this gives a positive spherical pivotal structure with the asserted FS signs and trace.

The positive pivotal curl on $D$ is fixed by partial trace: $\theta_D=(v(0)+v(1))/d=\beta(1-i)/d=\kappa/\beta$, since $\beta^2=\kappa(1+i)/d$. The group twists are $\theta_0=1$ and $\theta_\eta=-1$. Balancing holds in every channel: group-group crossings square to one; mixed crossings square to $-1=\theta_D/(\theta_\eta\theta_D)$; and on $DD$ one has $v(g)^2=\theta_g/\theta_D^2$ because $u(g)^2=\chi(g,g)=\theta_g$. All labels are self-dual and scalar twist equals its dual, so the ribbon condition holds. In particular the negative-sign parameters $\beta_-=-s^{-3}$ give $\theta_D=-1/\beta_-=s^3$, while the positive-sign parameters $\beta_+=s$ give $\theta_D=1/\beta_+=s^{-1}$; in both cases $\theta_\eta=-1$. This proves all normal-data, coherence, duality, pivotal, FS and ribbon claims.

Use all $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Put $V=\Delta(1)$ and let $P_0$ be its trivial-channel projector in $V\otimes V=\Delta(2)\oplus\Delta(0)$. The maps

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}),\qquad U_i\longmapsto\delta P_{0,i,i+1}$$

are well defined. Their composite with the negligible quotient has kernel exactly the embedded boundary ideal $I_n=(p_{\ell-1})$ and induces

$$\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)/I_n\ \cong\ \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}).$$

Equivalently the target is the full centralizer on a chosen sum of the retained tilting summands. The unreduced map does **not** kill $p_{\ell-1}$: its image is the nonzero simple $\Delta(\ell-1)$.

The precise categorical comparison is with the additive Karoubi negligible quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$, equipped with its ordinary diagram braiding $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ and with planar pivotal structure multiplied by tensor parity $(-1)^n$. This is ribbon-equivalent to $\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell$. Its endomorphism algebras are identified with positive-loop TL algebras by $U_i=-e_i$. Its pivotal dimensions are $[a+1]_q$, and its twists on retained labels are $s^{a(a+2)}$. The quantum self-duality cup/cap have loop $-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$, whereas the parity-corrected pivotal closure has value $+\delta$ on $V$. Thus no equivalence of the unmodified positive-loop unoriented **pivotal** TL category is asserted.

On the highest-weight-$2$ and trivial prequotient channels, the quantum crossing eigenvalues are $s,-s^{-3}$; the Hecke element $T_i=qU_i-1=-s c_i^{-1}$ has eigenvalues $-1,q^2$. The highest-weight-$2$ channel is retained only when $\ell\ge4$. Pivotal traces, twists and all framed ribbon closures agree under the stated corrected comparison. Assume countable choice only when invoking the cited free framed-tangle evaluation theorem; the local matrix and path arguments use no choice axiom.

For every $\ell\ge3$, the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] is rigid and braided by $c_{M,N}=\operatorname{flip}\circ R_{M,N}$, where

$$R_{M,N}=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E_M^{(r)}\otimes F_N^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$$

The sum is finite on every pair of objects. Its pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and its ribbon twist is $\theta_M=u_M^{-1}j_M$, with $u$ the Drinfeld map. For $V=\Delta(1)$, the self-dual cup and cap are

$$w=v_+\otimes v_- -q^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+,\qquad b(v_+\otimes v_-)=-q,\quad b(v_-\otimes v_+)=1,$$

with $b(v_\pm\otimes v_\pm)=0$. They obey both snakes, $b(w)=-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$ for $j$. Nevertheless $\dim_j V=\delta$. If $U=-wb$, then $U^2=\delta U$, the adjacent TL relations hold, and

$$c_{V,V}=sI-s^{-1}U,\qquad T=qU-I=-s\,c_{V,V}^{-1}.$$

The $\Delta(2)$ and trivial channels have crossing eigenvalues $s,-s^{-3}$ and Hecke eigenvalues $-1,q^2$, respectively. Their twists are $s^8,1$; $\theta_V=s^3I$. The $\Delta(2)$ channel is removed in the negligible quotient when $\ell=3$. More generally $\theta_{\Delta(a)}=s^{a(a+2)}I$ for $0\le a\le\ell-1$. These assertions include even $\ell$ and use no small-quantum-group substitution.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

For generic $q$, or whenever the quantum integers needed for $p_r,p_s,p_t$ are units, the unnormalized trivalent theta pairing satisfies

$$\Theta(r,s,t)=\frac{[m]![n']![p]![m+n'+p+1]!}{[m+n']![n'+p]![m+p]!},$$

where $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n'=(s+t-r)/2$, $p=(t+r-s)/2$ are nonnegative integers. The vertices and exact unit domain are those of [[lem-temperley-lieb-general-theta-net-evaluation]]. At $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, the pairing is positive when the triangle/parity conditions hold and $r+s+t\le2\ell-4$; it is zero for a triangle/parity triple above that level. A triple requiring an undefined root JW projector is not implicitly included.

Put $k=\ell-2$ and quotient the diagram category by the tensor ideal generated by $p_{k+1}$. A retained path of length $n$ is $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $a_0=0$, $0\le a_i\le k$ and $|a_i-a_{i-1}|=1$. There are inclusions $i_a:p_{a_n}\to n$ and retractions $r_a:n\to p_{a_n}$ such that $r_ai_b=0$ for distinct paths, $r_ai_a=p_{a_n}$, and $\sum_a i_ar_a=1_n$. Consequently the $E_{a,b}=i_ar_b$ at a common endpoint form complete matrix units, with

$$E_{a,b}E_{c,d}=\delta_{b,c}E_{a,d},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(E_{a,b})=\delta_{a,b}[a_n+1]_q.$$

Their pairing is nondegenerate. The endpoint $p_{k+1}$ is deleted before normalization; no denominator $[\ell]$ is used.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. Put

$$\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)=\{x\in\mathrm{TL}_n:\tau_n(xy)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathrm{TL}_n\}.$$

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by $p_{\ell-1}\otimes1_{n-\ell+1}$ for $n\ge\ell-1$, and $I_n=0$ below that rank. Then $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$, and $\mathrm{TL}_n/I_n$ is the direct sum of full matrix algebras with multiplicities given by length-$n$ paths from $0$ of heights $0,\ldots,\ell-2$. The additive idempotent-complete negligible quotient has simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$, represented by $p_a$, and

$$a\otimes b\cong\bigoplus_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}c.$$

At $n=\ell-1$ the unreduced algebra is semisimple, while its trace radical is the nonzero one-dimensional block generated by $p_{\ell-1}$. Trace radical and Jacobson radical are therefore distinct at this first boundary.

Let $a,b,c,d$ be simple charges in a unitary fusion category, and put
$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique
empty $0\times0$ matrix.

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects in a unitary braided fusion category, with
braiding $c_{a,b}:a\otimes b\to b\otimes a$ as in [[def-braiding]]. The typed
channel-exchange map on $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$ is the
pullback

$$\mathcal R_{ab}^c(f):=f\circ c_{a,b}^{-1}\in V_{ba}^c.$$

Choose orthonormal bases in the two multiplicity spaces. The matrix of
$\mathcal R_{ab}^c$ in these bases is the **R-symbol** $R_{ab}^c$. This
pullback convention fixes the orientation of the coordinate exchange; reversing
the braiding orientation replaces it by the inverse convention. If the spaces
are zero-dimensional, the braiding isomorphism identifies both with $0$ and
the R-symbol is the unique empty $0\times0$ matrix.

derivations.claim: Put $d=\sqrt2$, $q=e^{\pi i/4}$ and $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. In the specified root quotient the labels $p_0,p_1,p_2$ are $\mathbf1,D,\eta$. The fundamental FS sign is $-1$, positive pivotal dimension is $d$, twists are $\theta_D=s^3$, $\theta_\eta=-1$, and object crossing eigenvalues are $c_{DD}^0=-s^{-3}=e^{5\pi i/8}$ and $c_{DD}^\eta=s$.

The local definition of R is pullback $f\mapsto f\circ c_{a,b}^{-1}$. Consequently the displayed positive-Hadamard Ising sector phases correspond to object eigenvalues $e^{\pi i/8},e^{-3\pi i/8}$ and FS sign $+1$. Neither FS nor an equal-input braiding eigenvalue changes under a vertex gauge. These are therefore distinct categories, and the inverse-pullback orientation will force target twist $e^{-\pi i/8}$, not an implicitly imported physical twist $e^{\pi i/8}$.

Work in the root's negative-loop realization, with cup $w$, cap $b$, both snakes and $bw=-d$. Set $P=p_2=I+wb/d$, represent $D$ by one strand and $\eta$ by the two-strand summand $P$, and put $W_2=(I\otimes w\otimes I)w$, $B_2=b(I\otimes b\otimes I)$. Choose all unit vertices as identities and the nonunit inclusions/retractions as $\begin{aligned}i_{DD}^0&=w/\sqrt d,&p_{DD}^0&=-b/\sqrt d,\\i_{DD}^\eta&=P,&p_{DD}^\eta&=P,\\i_{\eta D}^D&=-\sqrt d(P\otimes I)(I\otimes w),&p_{\eta D}^D&=\sqrt d(I\otimes b)(P\otimes I),\\i_{D\eta}^D&=-\sqrt d(I\otimes P)(w\otimes I),&p_{D\eta}^D&=\sqrt d(b\otimes I)(I\otimes P),\\i_{\eta\eta}^0&=-(P\otimes P)W_2,&p_{\eta\eta}^0&=-B_2(P\otimes P).\end{aligned}$ The last minus sign is part of the gauge: omitting it would change four scalar F blocks. The positive unitary dagger has $w^\dagger=-b$; it is not the ordinary Hilbert adjoint of matrices in the quantum weight basis.

The snakes, $P^2=P$, $Pw=bP=0$ and $d^2=2$ prove these are isometric splittings. For example, for $A=(P\otimes I)(I\otimes w)$ one has $A^\dagger=-(I\otimes b)(P\otimes I)$ and $A^\dagger A=1/d$, so $-\sqrt d A$ is isometric; reflection proves the other mixed case. The nested two-strand cup/cap contraction with $P$ inserted is one, proving the $\eta\eta$ normalization. The channel projections sum to identity in the negligible quotient: $DD$ is vacuum plus $P$, $\eta D$ and $D\eta$ are simple $D$ after killing $p_3$, and $\eta\eta$ is the unit. In the constructed three-simple category the second-pair vacuum coefficient on the first-pair $\eta$ part of its $DDD$ fusion space is $1/2$, so the corresponding $U_2=dP_{\mathrm{vac}}$ sandwich is $1/d$ and $p_3=(P\otimes I)-d(P\otimes I)U_2(P\otimes I)=0$. This concerns the quotient, not the nonzero unreduced weight-module projector.

Every F entry is the same explicit contraction $(p_{af}^z)(1_a\otimes p_{bc}^f)(i_{ab}^e\otimes1_c)i_{ec}^z=F_z^{abc}[f,e]1_z$, where $1_\eta=P$, $1_D=I$, $1_0=1$ and every elementary multiplicity coordinate equals one. With the gauge of step 3.1 the full nonunit table is $\begin{array}{c|c|c}(a,b,c)&z&F_z^{abc}\\(\eta,\eta,\eta)&\eta&1\\(\eta,\eta,D)&D&1\\(\eta,D,\eta)&D&-1\\(D,\eta,\eta)&D&1\\(\eta,D,D)&0,\eta&1,1\\(D,\eta,D)&0,\eta&1,-1\\(D,D,\eta)&0,\eta&1,1\\(D,D,D)&D&d^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}\end{array}$. Unit blocks are identities and impossible channels are empty. Thus every coefficient, rather than only a selected sector, has a specified matrix product and basis.

Expand $P=1+wb/d$ in those contractions. Each inner cup-cap contributes $-d$ or is removed by a snake; turnbacks into $P$ vanish. In the two-dimensional block the left/right vacuum overlap is $-1/d$, the fixed negative mixed inclusions make both off-diagonal overlaps $-1/d$, and normalization/orthogonality gives the final overlap $+1/d$. In scalar blocks expanding a $P$ next to a mixed vertex either removes its turnback term or leaves its complementary $1/d$ term. The chosen minus on $i_{\eta\eta}^0$ cancels precisely the otherwise negative blocks $\eta\eta D$, $D\eta\eta$, $\eta DD$ of total zero and $DD\eta$ of total zero. The remaining scalar signs are exactly $\eta D\eta$ and $D\eta D$ of total $\eta$. This proves step 5.1's full table and matches the normal category at $\kappa=-1$. An independent exact-matrix evaluation uses $q=(1+i)/\sqrt2$, $w=(0,1,-q^{-1},0)^{\mathsf t}$ and $b=(0,-q,1,0)$ in the same contractions, extracting the scalar on the highest retained vector; it corroborates all 33 admissible F blocks, rather than supplying a missing argument.

The category identification also follows directly from the tensor functor generated by cup $\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$ and cap $-\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$ in the negative-sign normal category. They satisfy both snakes and loop $-d$, so define a functor from negative-loop TL; $p_2$ maps to $\eta$ and $p_3$ maps to zero by step 4.1. The complete retained path matrix units give full faithfulness on every tensor power and rectangular Hom block: both sides have the same $A_3$ paths, scalar corners $0,D,\eta$, and nonzero normalized splits, and these generate all objects. The positive pivotal structures agree in dimension and the actual negative FS convention. The explicit maps of step 3.1 fix its vertex gauge, so this is a category equivalence rather than merely a fusion-ring identification. The matching braiding in the next step makes it a ribbon equivalence.

At $\kappa=-1$, take $\beta_-=-s^{-3}$. Then $\beta_-^2=-(1+i)/d$ and $v(1)=-i\beta_-=s$. The negative-loop source crossing $sI+s^{-1}e$ agrees with both actual root $DD$ eigenvalues. Since $D$ generates and the hexagons build every block crossing, the full root braiding is the normal table: $c_{\eta\eta}^0=-1$ and $c_{\eta D}^D=c_{D\eta}^D=i$, together with those two $DD$ entries and unit entries one. Contractions of the explicit block crossings with step 3.1's vertices give the same ten channels. The full normal-data supplier proves the positive pivot and curl $\theta_D=-1/\beta_-=s^3$, so step 7.1's equivalence preserves the specified ribbon structure.

Declare $D$ odd and the group objects even. Change the associator by $\omega(x,y,z)=(-1)^{xyz}$ on parities and the braiding by $\zeta^{xy}$ with $\zeta=-i$. The cocycle equation is the equality modulo two of $bcd+a(b+c)d+abc$ and $(a+b)cd+ab(c+d)$. It changes only the $DDD$ associator, hence flips $\tau$. The abelian hexagon correction uses $\zeta^2=-1$: an all-odd triple contributes the two crossing factors $\zeta^2$ and the compensating associator sign $-1$; all other parity placements contribute one. Equivalently the complete normal F/R table proves these changed hexagons entrywise. This is a parity associator change, not a vertex gauge.

Keep the $D$ coevaluation and flip its evaluation. The changed odd-triple associator flips its snake sign too, so both snakes remain identities and $\kappa$ changes from $-1$ to $+1$ while the positive pivotal dimension remains $d$. The mixed braidings stay $i$ and $\beta_+=(-i)\beta_-=s$. The positive curl changes by the same factor: $\theta_D^+=(-i)\theta_D^-=s^{-1}$. The normal supplier's explicit dual and double-dual tensorators verify this positive pivotal convention globally; it has not been chosen merely from the square of a braiding phase.

The resulting full pullback table is $R_{DD}^0=s^{-1}=e^{-\pi i/8}$, $R_{DD}^\eta=is^{-1}=e^{3\pi i/8}$, $R_{\eta D}^D=R_{D\eta}^D=-i$, $R_{\eta\eta}^0=-1$, and unit entries one. Its $DDD$ block is the positive Hadamard and its FS sign is $+1$, so it matches the stated inverse-pullback sector convention in the full coherent category. The root and changed categories retain their different associators, FS and braid phases. If object braiding phases $e^{-\pi i/8},e^{3\pi i/8}$ and twist $e^{\pi i/8}$ are instead desired, one must additionally reverse this braiding and invert its twist. That is a further explicit chirality operation, not the orientation of the local inverse-pullback definition. This proves all root-gauge and conversion assertions.

Put $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{0,1\}$, with $0=\mathbf1$, $1=\eta$, and a third simple $D$. Use $ab=a+b$, $aD=Da=D$, and $DD=0\oplus1$, with summands ordered $(0,1)$ and every nonzero elementary fusion multiplicity equal to one. Let $d=\sqrt2$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$, $\tau=\kappa/d$, $\chi(a,b)=(-1)^{ab}$, $u(0)=1$, $u(1)=i$, and choose $\beta$ of modulus one with $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. There is a unitary skeletal spherical ribbon fusion category with canonical orthonormal summand vertices and the following complete normal data. All admissible one-dimensional F blocks are $1$, except $F_D^{\eta D\eta}=F_\eta^{D\eta D}=-1$, and
$$F_D^{DDD}=\frac\kappa{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Rows are right-tree channels $(f,1,1)$ and columns left-tree channels $(e,1,1)$ in the inverse-precomposition convention. Unit blocks are identities and impossible channels have the unique empty matrix. The associator permutes the $DD$ summand by addition of a group input when needed; its complete formula and pentagon are proved below.

The object braiding is $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $c_{a,D}=c_{D,a}=u(a)$, and $c_{D,D}^g=\beta/u(g)$. The pullback R symbols are their inverses, in the specified canonical vertices. Both hexagons hold in every channel. The normalized self-duality has $\operatorname{coev}_D=\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$, $\operatorname{ev}_D=\kappa\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$, FS sign $\kappa$, positive pivotal dimension $d$, and twist $\theta_D=\kappa/\beta$; $\eta$ has dimension and FS sign one and twist $-1$. The canonical left-dual tensorator is $\kappa$ on both $DD$ channels and one on all other channels; its double-dual tensorator is one on all ten admissible channels. Relative to those duals $j_D=\kappa$, $j_0=j_\eta=1$, and $j_{a\otimes b}=\nu_{a,b}(j_a\otimes j_b)$ holds channel by channel. For explicit phase specializations write $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. These assertions construct the full category; they do not assume a sector example as a supplier.

$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects of a unitary fusion category
$\mathcal C$ ([[def-qc-tqc-unitary-fusion-category]]). The **fusion
multiplicity** is

$$N_{ab}^c:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c),$$

and the corresponding **fusion multiplicity space** is

$$V_{ab}^c:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c).$$

Since $c$ is absolutely simple
([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]), each $f,g\in V_{ab}^c$ has a unique scalar
$\langle f,g\rangle$ satisfying
$f\circ g^\dagger=\langle f,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$. This fixes the
inner-product convention to be linear in the first variable. The next local
theorem proves that this pairing is positive definite. No multiplicity-free
assumption is made: $N_{ab}^c$ may be any nonnegative integer.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

derivations.claim: A periodic length-$L$ path is $(x_1,\ldots,x_L)$ with $x_iD\supset x_{i+1}$ and $x_{L+1}=x_1$. Every elementary fusion index equals one and is retained. Fusion forces alternation between $D$ and $G$, so the space is zero for odd $L$. For $L=2N$, $N\ge1$, it is the orthogonal sum $H\oplus\bar H$, with $H$ given by $x_{2j-1}=D$, $x_{2j}=b_j\in G$ and $\bar H$ by $x_{2j-1}=b_j\in G$, $x_{2j}=D$. The $N$ bits are independent even across the wrap edge, giving dimension $2^N$ in each sector. The maps $\Phi_H,\Phi_{\bar H}$ send the paths to the standard orthonormal basis $|b_1\cdots b_N\rangle$, with inverse obtained by inserting the fixed $D$ labels. This includes both sectors without a total-flux or global-spin-parity projection; at $N=1$ there are four states.

Define $P_i$ to project the two reference edges from $x_i$ to $x_{i+2}$ to vacuum, changing only the intermediate label $x_{i+1}$. Its local F matrix is $F_{x_{i+2}}^{x_iDD}$, with source channel $x_{i+1}$ and target $DD$ output. Thus its index differs from a convention naming the intermediate link by one. If both neighbors are $D$, the F matrix is $\kappa$ times Hadamard and $F^{-1}\Pi_0F=(I+X)/2$ on the intermediate bit. If they are group labels $g,h$, the intermediate label is forced to be $D$ and the $DD$ output is $g+h$, so the vacuum projector is $\delta_{g,h}$. The overall $\kappa$ cancels, so both coherent sign conventions give the same projectors.

With bit indices modulo $N$, the complete sector images are $\Phi_HP_{2j-1}\Phi_H^{-1}=(I+X_j)/2$, $\Phi_HP_{2j}\Phi_H^{-1}=(I+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2$, $\Phi_{\bar H}P_{2j-1}\Phi_{\bar H}^{-1}=(I+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2$, and $\Phi_{\bar H}P_{2j}\Phi_{\bar H}^{-1}=(I+X_{j+1})/2$. This includes the wraparound edge. At $N=1$ the bond is $(I+Z_1^2)/2=I$ and the field is $(I+X_1)/2$. No three-distinct-site cyclic TL relation is asserted for that length-two identification; the ordinary interior theorem keeps its own applicable-index hypothesis.

Define the path shift by $(Tx)_i=x_{i+1}$ cyclically and let $C|b_1\cdots b_N\rangle=|b_2\cdots b_Nb_1\rangle$.
